t: You're on Gloucester Terrace, a street in Westminster, close to Paddington and Bayswater. It starts near Lancaster Gate tube station and Hyde Park, then curves north to meet Porchester Square. Westbourne Terrace runs parallel to the east, and at the northern end the railway and the Westway are close by. Two people were born on this street: Andrew Clark, who lived from 1847 to 1913 and became honorary surgeon to King George the Fifth, and Anthea Lascelles, who lived from 1930 to 1976.
